title: Priority Queue Shedding
description: Drops low-priority requests first when queue depth exceeds the shed watermark. Requests carry a priority class, and the shedder walks from lowest to highest until the queue fits the budget. Critical traffic survives overloads that would otherwise take everything down.
key_mechanisms: Tag requests with priority classes
Shed lowest priority first past the watermark
Return 429 with retry guidance for shed work

demo.title: Demo — Priority Queue Shedding

title: Circuit Breaker Tripping
description: Opens the breaker after N consecutive failures, shedding downstream calls until the dependency recovers. While open, calls fail fast instead of piling up threads against a dead service. Half-open probes test recovery before full traffic resumes.
key_mechanisms: Count consecutive failures per dependency
Open the breaker past the threshold
Probe with half-open requests before closing

demo.title: Demo — Circuit Breaker Tripping

title: Token Bucket Admission
description: Admits only requests holding a token; excess is shed with 429 instead of queuing. Tokens refill at a fixed rate, so bursts are absorbed up to the bucket size and sustained overload is rejected cleanly. It bounds resource use with a single simple mechanism.
key_mechanisms: Refill tokens at the configured rate
Require one token per request
Reject excess with 429, never queue unboundedly

demo.title: Demo — Token Bucket Admission

title: Graceful Degradation Tiers
description: Serves reduced-fidelity responses — no images, cached data, simplified layouts — under load instead of failing. Tier selection is driven by live health signals, and the system steps down and back up automatically. Users get a slower but working product during peaks.
key_mechanisms: Define fidelity tiers per endpoint
Step down tiers on health signals
Restore full fidelity as load recedes

demo.title: Demo — Graceful Degradation Tiers

title: Request Hedging
description: Sends a duplicate request after p99 latency and keeps whichever returns first, shedding the loser. Hedging trades a little extra load for dramatically better tail latency. It must be used carefully — hedged retries during a true overload make things worse.
key_mechanisms: Start a timer at p99 on each request
Fire a duplicate when the timer expires
Cancel the loser and keep the winner

demo.title: Demo — Request Hedging

title: Backpressure Propagation
description: Pushes slow-consumer signals upstream so producers shed or slow before buffers explode. Reactive streams make backpressure a first-class signal: each stage requests only what it can handle. Without it, fast producers drown slow consumers in unbounded queues.
key_mechanisms: Signal demand upstream per stage
Bound all inter-stage buffers
Shed or slow producers on pressure

demo.title: Demo — Backpressure Propagation

title: Adaptive Rate Limiting
description: Adjusts per-client limits from live server health instead of static quotas. When the server is healthy, well-behaved clients get generous limits; as health degrades, limits tighten automatically. It replaces one-size-fits-all throttling with a control loop.
key_mechanisms: Measure server health continuously
Scale per-client limits with health
Prioritize well-behaved clients

demo.title: Demo — Adaptive Rate Limiting

title: Queue-Depth Shedding
description: Sheds new work when internal queues pass 80 percent capacity, protecting in-flight requests. It is better to reject new work fast than to accept it and fail everything slowly. The watermark is set below the point where latency starts climbing.
key_mechanisms: Monitor queue depth against a watermark
Reject new work past 80% capacity
Protect in-flight requests first

demo.title: Demo — Queue-Depth Shedding

title: CPU-Throttle Shedding
description: Drops non-critical background tasks when CPU steal time rises on edge nodes. Telemetry sync, log shipping, and model updates pause while user-facing work keeps its cores. Tasks resume automatically when headroom returns.
key_mechanisms: Watch CPU steal and pressure stall metrics
Pause background task classes on pressure
Resume automatically with headroom

demo.title: Demo — CPU-Throttle Shedding

title: Memory-Pressure Eviction
description: Evicts caches proactively under memory pressure to avoid OOM kills. The evictor ranks caches by value-per-byte and drops the cheapest first, keeping hot data resident. It turns sudden OOM crashes into graceful, predictable degradation.
key_mechanisms: Rank caches by value per byte
Evict cheapest caches under pressure
Pre-size caches to avoid the cliff

demo.title: Demo — Memory-Pressure Eviction

title: Deadline-Aware Dropping
description: Drops requests whose deadlines already expired instead of wasting compute on them. Each request carries a deadline, and the scheduler checks it before spending CPU. It is the highest-ROI shedding rule in latency-sensitive pipelines.
key_mechanisms: Propagate deadlines with every request
Check deadlines before spending compute
Count expired drops as a health metric

demo.title: Demo — Deadline-Aware Dropping

title: Fair-Share Shedding
description: Sheds proportionally across tenants so one abusive client cannot starve the others. Each tenant gets a fair share of capacity, and excess is shed from whoever is over their share. It keeps multi-tenant systems usable during one tenant's traffic spike.
key_mechanisms: Track per-tenant usage vs fair share
Shed from tenants over their share
Protect tenants under their share

demo.title: Demo — Fair-Share Shedding

title: Brownout Patterns
description: Probabilistically disables optional features — recommendations, previews, rich media — as load climbs. A brownout controller dials feature probability from 100 to 0 percent with rising load, shedding expensive work smoothly. Users notice slightly less richness, not errors.
key_mechanisms: Rank features by cost and optionality
Dial feature probability with load
Restore features as load recedes

demo.title: Demo — Brownout Patterns

title: Overload Classifiers
description: Uses an ML classifier to predict overload 30 seconds ahead from metrics and pre-shed. Trained on historical incidents, it spots the metric signature of an incoming overload before queues fill. Pre-shedding buys the system time to scale or degrade gracefully.
key_mechanisms: Train on historical overload signatures
Score live metrics every few seconds
Pre-shed when overload probability is high

demo.title: Demo — Overload Classifiers

title: Shed Auditing
description: Logs every shed decision with reason codes for post-incident analysis. Without an audit trail, nobody can tell whether a shed was correct or a bug; with one, teams tune watermarks from evidence. Audit records include the signal values that triggered the shed.
key_mechanisms: Log every shed with reason codes
Record the triggering signal values
Review shed logs after incidents
